observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be
live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtuaJMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to bsaleaumua@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak and
downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Corona virus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state oflocal emergency.
In order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the Commission meeting will be open and
public but conducted virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to the
health or safety of attendees. This way, the public, the staff, and the Commission will not be
physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which
are not listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although
no action may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items
needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes. Members of the public wishing to speak
during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to
speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be
present in the Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https"://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and
follow the directions for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are
not subject to public discvssion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may b~ removed from the Consent Calendar for individual
consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so
declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the
Consent Calendar will be taken .up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been
submitted. Public speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items whkh are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public
comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing

Subject:  Malibu City Gallery Exhibition Schedule

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Review and approve the Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad
Hoc Committee's recommended Art Exhibitions at the Malibu City Gallery for Fiscal Year
2023-2024.

DISCUSSION: The Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad Hoc Committee (Ad Hoc Committee),
consisting of Vice Chair Lawrence and Commissioner Holland, prepared a list of six art
exhibitions for the 2023-2024 Malibu City Gallery Exhibition Schedule. The proposed list
of exhibitions includes:

  •  Multi-Artist Exhibition; All Mediums
  •  Dick Van Dyke Tribute Exhibition; All Mediums
  •  Student Art Exhibition; All Mediums
  •  Single Artist Exhibition; To Be Determined
  •  Leigh McClosky; Emerging Renaissance
  •  Multi-Artist Exhibition ; All Mediums; Theme: Surf Culture

Dick Van Dyke Tribute
Dick Van Dyke is an actor, comedian, and longtime Malibu resident. Known for his charm,
comedic timing, and physical comedy, Mr. Van Dyke is considered a beloved Malibu
treasure . His artistic achievements include a Kennedy Center honoree, five Emmys, a
Tony, a Grammy, the SAG Lifetime Achievement Award, introduction into the Television
Hall of Fame, and several other honors. Mr. Van Dyke will provide artwork from various
artists consisting of portraits and art featuring his theatrical and musical works.

Student Art Exhibition
The City typically hosts the annual Malibu Student Art Exhibition in February. The
Community Services Department coordinates the Student Art Exhibition in partnership

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item # 5.A.
 with the Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission and typically displays over 200
pieces of student artwork.

Leigh Mcclosky
Leigh McClosky is an artist, actor, and visual Hermetic philosopher. His life, career, and
art reveal in beauty and meaning his devotion to the ideal of cultivation renaissance and
creative rebirth through a shared enthusiasm of inspiring stories of being human. He has
written, illustrated, and published seven books and many articles. Mr. McClosky was born
and raised in Malibu and returned in 1982. He hosts weekly discussion groups and
public/private events at his Malibu home.

Surf Culture
Since 2022, the Commission has curated a summer exhibition related to Malibu surf
culture due to the popularity of a previous exhibition in 2016, The Art of the Board. The
exhibitions in 2022 and 2023 have featured several local and regional artists. Due to
Malibu's influential surf culture and history, the Commission recommended future
exhibition schedules include at least one surf-related exhibition each year.

In addition to the four exhibitions described above, the Ad Hoc also recommends hosting
two additional exhibitions.

  •  Multi-Artist Exhibition
  •  Single Artist Exhibition

The exhibitions will be open to the public from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, Monday through
Friday, at the Malibu City Gallery in City Hall. Funding for the exhibitions, including
marketing, online art call submission fees, and supplies, were included in the Adopted
Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-2024. The Ad Hoc Committee will curate and coordinate the
programs related to each exhibition and provide updates during Commission Regular
meetings.

Subject:  Art Loan Agreement with Anna Kelly

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Determine whether to extend the loan agreement with
artist Anna Kelly for her painting Saving Malibu; and 2) Provide a recommendation to the
City Council regarding the donation.

DISCUSSION: On September 28, 2021 , the Commission approved a request from artist
Anna Kelly to display her painting, Saving Malibu at Malibu City Hall Multipurpose Room
(Attachment 1). Rather than accepting the artwork as a donation, the Commission
recommended the City enter into a one-year loan agreement with the artist.

City Council approved the Commission's recommendation on November 8, 2021 , and
entered into a loan agreement with Ms. Kelly on July 12, 2022.

Staff notified Ms. Kelly that the loan agreement term would end on July 12, 2023, and
she requested an additional one-year extension . If the Commission recommends
extending the loan agreement for one year, the new term will expire on July 12, 2024.

The Commission is asked to review the request from Ms. Kelly and make a
recommendation regarding the loan agreement term. If the Commission approves a
recommendation, City Council will review the loan agreement at an upcoming meeting
for final approval .

  ATTACHMENT 1
   Saving Malibu
  Artist Anna Kelly

  Artist Statement

Art speaks with a powerful voice, and can awaken us to the wonder of being alive
in this world. Since antiquity, poetry, music, and painting have been used to
express feelings and record events.

For decades, my fellow artists and I have painted in many locales around Malibu,
from Malibu Creek State Park to the city's beaches. When the Woolsey Fire broke
out, and we saw these areas of natural beauty in flames, we were heartbroken.

"Saving Malibu" was painted between 2019 and 2021 to salute the courage of the
firefighters who risked their lives for Malibu.

My thanks to these bra.ve firefighters from the bottom of my heart. Your sacrifice
will never be forgotten!

Artist Anna T. Kelly
September 2021

  B.  Art Loan Agreement with Anna Kelly
  Recommended Action: 1) Determine whether to extend the loan agreement with
  Artist Anna Kelly for her painting Saving Malibu, and 2) Provide a
  recommendation to the City Council regarding the donation.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Cherin rejoined the meeting at 10:05 a.m.

  Commissioner Jones stated he was satisfied with the one-year loan agreement and
  recommended not to extend the agreement. He stated the standard term for an art
  loan agreement should be one year.

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated disagreement with Commissioner Jones and
  recommended extending the agreement.

  Commissioner Jones stated a one-year loan agreement would allow the
  Commission to consider an annual art rotation. He stated the Commission should
  adopt an art loan or donation policy.

  Chair Lawrence and  Commissioner  Cherin  indicated  agreement  with
  Commissioner Jones.

  Vice Chair Holland suggested adding art hanging hardware in the hallways and
  multipurpose room at City Hall.

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated agreement with Vice Chair Holland.

  In response to Chair Lawrence, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  artwork could be installed in one additional location in the multipurpose room. She
  stated the Commission should decide to replace the artwork or extend the current
  agreement with Ms. Kelly.
